scope: One sourced epigraph for each of the five content lessons. Welcome and the shared glossary are navigation/reference pages.
presentation: Native Markdown blockquote with Thai translation, source-language excerpt, author and direct source link; existing fonts and theme tokens; no assets or motion.
translation_credit: Thai translations newly written for QuantCorner; source-language quotations clearly separated.
preservation: The separate pre-existing Thai opening remark in random-assets.md is preserved without inventing attribution.

quotes.author: Louis Bachelier
quotes.label: Théorie de la spéculation (1900), น. 21
quotes.note: Opening clause of the introduction, with an ellipsis marking the omitted continuation. Original French was inspected in the scanned paper.
quotes.relation: Many influences on asset prices; uncertainty motivates probabilistic models.

quotes.author: Richard Feynman
quotes.label: ข้อความบนกระดานของ Feynman · Caltech
quotes.note: Caltech reports the exact words on the blackboard left in his office in 1988. Used as an analogy about learning by construction, not a statement he made about the binomial model.
quotes.relation: Build the tree and replicating portfolio to understand option pricing.

quotes.author: Pierre-Simon Laplace
quotes.label: A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities, น. 196
quotes.note: English translation by F. W. Truscott and F. L. Emory, 1902. A clause excerpt; the ellipsis explicitly omits “at bottom”. The surrounding passage was checked in chapter XVIII. Thai translation is newly written by QuantCorner.
quotes.relation: Translate intuitive questions about future outcomes into probability densities and integrals.

quotes.author: Henri Poincaré
quotes.label: The Value of Science, บท I §V
quotes.note: Exact two sentences in the English translation in The Foundations of Science, translated by George Bruce Halsted. The word rôle and sentence boundaries are retained. This is a general mathematical reflection, not a quotation about Itô calculus specifically.
quotes.relation: Connect path intuition and rigorous limiting arguments when learning stochastic calculus.

quotes.author: George E. P. Box
quotes.label: Robustness in the Strategy of Scientific Model Building (1979)
quotes.note: Exact uppercase section heading in the original report, verified using the public DTIC archive full text. Also independently corroborated by the University of Wisconsin–Madison Department of Statistics. Not a claim that assumptions can be ignored.
quotes.relation: Use Black–Scholes with an understanding of its assumptions, usefulness and limits.
